unit.why: A quotation from Ketem Ofir on ulterior motives (peniyot) in mitzvot. It is illustrated by a one-sentence exemplum of a soul-ascent encounter in Gan Eden, followed by the closing formula of section 3 and the heading of section 4 on devekut.
unit.boundary_note: The division ends with the heading of the next section ('מענין דביקות'), whose first story begins in the next division.

stories.summary_en: During an ascent of the soul to Gan Eden, the master (מרן) asked a soul what was wrong with it. It answered that the rewards for its mitzvot give off a bad smell, because it did everything with ulterior motives.

tags.why: The encounter takes place during an aliyat neshamah.
The scene is set in Gan Eden.
The master converses with a departed soul.

quotes: אזי יש להם ריח רע מחמת שעשיתי הכל בפניות
tags.why: The soul's reward is spoiled as a consequence of its ulterior motives.
The anecdote is embedded in an exegetical comment on Esther, which forms its homiletic frame.
The point is the moral value of performing mitzvot without ulterior motives.

missing_concepts: the smell of mitzvot / reward in the afterlife
